### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a08fec2c639db674dade37655b32c6f1738e1a22` — the merge of head `922bc3dd66cce58dc28d81dd512c4f651f6ff610` into base `b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a08fec2c639db674dade37655b32c6f1738e1a22 && git checkout a08fec2c639db674dade37655b32c6f1738e1a22
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83 922bc3dd66cce58dc28d81dd512c4f651f6ff610 && git checkout -B drift-repro b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83 && git merge --no-ff 922bc3dd66cce58dc28d81dd512c4f651f6ff610

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `922bc3dd66cce58dc28d81dd512c4f651f6ff610`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.test.ts, .changeset/30633-flow-input-declaration-lint.md (the whole non-prose diff; the start-admission code it cites on `main`, `packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts` and `isObjectLessActionKey`, was read, not reviewed)

The face is the declaration alone: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and changeset, with no published schema and no governed path in the diff. Governing text: card #30633 (filed from contract record 6666908076 ④ items 2–3), claim 6672120182 with amendments 6672887535, 6673479741 and 6674671434, dev report 6673465151. Read-only: the diff at this head and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface.** The `@objectstack/lint` barrel gains two names, `FLOW_INPUT_OBJECT_LESS` and `FLOW_INPUT_RECORD_READ_AS_LIST`, string rule-id constants beside the existing `FLOW_INPUT_UNKNOWN_OBJECT`. Nothing is removed or retyped. **Widening, as declared.**
2. **Nothing narrows.** Both new findings are `warning` severity, in the advisory family of 1i; no path makes either an error, and no stack that validated before is refused. `flow-input-unknown-object` keeps its verdicts (the 1j block is additive and leaves `declaredInputs` local). **Right.**
3. **`flow-input-object-less`** fires on `objectName` in the object-less key set `global` and `*`, mirrored by hand from `isObjectLessActionKey`, the same lockstep convention `stack.zod.ts` uses for `GLOBAL_ACTION_SCOPE`. It is judged on every variable that carries `objectName`; since the schema refuses `objectName` on a non-input at parse, that is the start inputs in practice. **Right.**
4. **`flow-input-record-read-as-list`** reads the way start admission reads: only an `isInput` variable, only `get_record` / `update_record` / `delete_record` with a literal `objectName`, only a `filter.id.$in` that hands the input on unchanged (a CEL envelope whose source is the bare name or `vars.` name), and not where a `loop` or `map` rebinds the name. The walk is `walkFlowNodes`, so nested branches are covered. A list read through a `subflow` or `map` hand-off is not judged, and the comment says so. **Right, and conservative: it can miss, it cannot misfire on a computed value.**
5. **Explanation text.** The `flow-input-unknown-object` paragraph and the 1i docblock and message move to the present tense now that PR #30628 enforces the declaration, and the "planned" sentence is gone. No tracker number reaches a runtime string (`check:doc-authoring`). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/lint`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. The level follows the metadata-protocol line alone (ruling A on #25105, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`); two lint rule ids are not part of the protocol an author writes against. The declaration lines are identical in body and changeset and read as `yes` / `widening` and `none`. **Check Changeset** is green on this head. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []`. Deviations: the `Clause-②` line was `no` on the claim and the first heads, corrected to `yes (widening)` at this head and on the claim by amendment 6674671434. No other deviation. Author note: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

1. **Pins.** The test file only adds cases (no existing line is edited). Object-less: `global` warns beside the unknown-object verdict, still warns where the stack defines an object named `global`, `*` warns, and a defined object is silent. Read-as-list: a `$in` hand-off warns at the read naming input, node and both objects; a `vars.` hand-off inside a nested region warns at the nested node. Silent cases: `filter.id` and `filter.id.$eq` reads, an undeclared input, a non-input, a computed `$in` source, a `loop` that rebinds the name, and a non-addressing `create_record` node. Each names a distinct branch of the 1j block. A `map` item rebinding is not pinned on its own (it shares the `loop` branch).
2. **Tried to break it.** Two declared inputs with the same name: the first wins, which matches the schema's own uniqueness. A `$in` holding a literal array: `handedOnVariable` returns undefined, so no finding. An `objectName` of `''`: `nonEmptyString` drops it, and the schema refuses it anyway. A loop whose iterator shadows a declared input: the input is dropped from the read check for the whole flow. That can miss a real read outside the loop, but it never misfires, which is the right direction for an advisory. No must-fix.
3. **Gates.** Every check-run on this head has concluded: 56 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure.

Should-fix (non-blocking): `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` ("The name is checked", near :2212) names only `flow-input-unknown-object`. The two new warnings could be taught there; the sentence is not false, so this is a follow-up, not a fix here.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-30633-flow-input-objectname-lint`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cytLmJxfAmgPVjUbbW`

**VERDICT: PASS**
